author: delegate-eval
title: Close texting for candidates within 19 days of their general election
body:
ClickUp: https://app.clickup.com/t/17tnw2b4zn5

## Why

Texting verification takes about two weeks to clear campaign verification and carrier review. Candidates who joined late were still being pushed into texting setup that could not finish before their election. Each of them did the work, often paid for Pro partly for texting, and found out too late. We also paid for a website, a domain and a Peerly registration for every one of them, for nothing. With the Oct. 15 cutoff for Nov. 3 races, this needed to stop now.

## Why this was reworked

Bryan's review of the first version and Jared's note in Slack both said it announced the cutoff too loudly and too late. Candidates who had already upgraded were told texting "needs registration" instead of simply that the deadline had passed, and the explanation reached candidates after they bought Pro instead of before. Jared also asked to keep the campaign filing page as it was: there is no harm in still collecting filing details, and the Pro wizard still needs them to confirm the candidate is legitimate.

So the cutoff now shows only where it matters: a short reason on hover ("The Oct. 15 deadline to get verified for texting has passed."), a small banner on the Pro wizard's guidance step before purchase, and a countdown in the week before. Filing details are still collected after the cutoff. gp-api saves them but never starts the paid compliance run.

## The rule

gp-api owns one rule and the webapp reads it. It never does date math of its own.

- Texting closes 19 days before the campaign's general election (`details.electionDate`), at the end of the cutoff day, Eastern time. A Nov. 3 race stays open through 11:59 pm ET on Oct. 15 and closes at 12:00 am ET on Oct. 16. The week before the cutoff reads as "closing" and shows a countdown.
- To make the cutoff you must have filed AND paid before it, which means `kickoffSentAt` is set. Verification only starts at payment, so details saved without paying do not count.
- Internal-testing approvals count as having made the cutoff.
- No general election date leaves texting open, as it is today.

Once the window is closed, the agentic filing submit still saves the record, but an already-Pro campaign's kickoff is skipped and logged. The legacy synchronous compliance submit, the agent's Peerly submission and a text purchase are refused with a 409 `SMS_COMPLIANCE_CUTOFF`, and the payment webhook and the stranded-kickoff sweep skip the kickoff.

## Where this differs from the ticket

- The outreach events are named `Outreach - SMS Cutoff Notice Viewed` and `Outreach - SMS Cutoff Notice Completed`, not `Voter Outreach - ...`, to follow the analytics naming rule.
- The plan's text sends inside the window will be dropped in Phase 2, not swapped for another channel. A swap needs a new catalog entry.
- There is no per-campaign override. A wrong election date is fixed by editing it in gp-admin, which already exists.

## Use-client baseline

`check:use-client` goes from 591 to 593. `SmsCutoffNotice` fires its viewed event from an effect and tracks the channel a candidate picks, and `useSmsCompliance` reads the campaign through the client campaign context, so neither can be a server component.

## Follow-ups

- Phase 2 per the plan: pitch copy across the Pro and outreach surfaces, dropping text sends inside the window from the tracker and campaign plan, and the Campaign Manager's texting context.
- Amplitude event metadata for the new events is not recorded yet.
- The HubSpot 10DLC workflows that nudge non-compliant candidates need cutoff suppression from CRM ops.

 }
 
+export const SMS_CUTOFF_LEAD_DAYS = 19
+export const SMS_CUTOFF_CLOSING_DAYS = 7
+export const SMS_COMPLIANCE_CUTOFF_ERROR_CODE = 'SMS_COMPLIANCE_CUTOFF'
+
+const DAY_MS = 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000
+
+// A candidate "made the cutoff" only once they filed AND paid, which is when
+// kickoffSentAt is stamped. A compliance record saved without payment does not
+// count, so that candidate gets the date-based window like anyone else.
+// Internal-testing approvals never kick off, so they count as made.
+export const smsComplianceWindow = ({
+  electionDate,
+  tcrCompliance,
+  now,
+}: {
+  electionDate: string | null | undefined
+  tcrCompliance: {
+    kickoffSentAt: Date | null
+    internalTestingAt?: Date | null
+  } | null
+  now: Date
+}): {
+  smsCompliance: SmsComplianceWindow
+  smsCutoffDate: string | null
+  generalElectionDate: string | null
+} => {
+  const parsed = electionDate ? parseIsoDateAsUTC(electionDate) : null
+  const election = parsed && isValid(parsed) ? getMidnightForDate(parsed) : null
+  const generalElectionDate = toDateOnlyString(election) ?? null
+  const smsCutoffDate = election
+    ? (toDateOnlyString(
+        new Date(election.getTime() - SMS_CUTOFF_LEAD_DAYS * DAY_MS),
+      ) ?? null)
+    : null
+
+  if (tcrCompliance?.kickoffSentAt || tcrCompliance?.internalTestingAt) {
+    return {
+      smsCompliance: 'not_applicable',
+      smsCutoffDate,
+      generalElectionDate,
+    }
+  }
+  if (!election) {
+    return { smsCompliance: 'open', smsCutoffDate, generalElectionDate }
+  }
+
+  // The cutoff day lasts until midnight Eastern, so "today" is the calendar
+  // day in ET, set at UTC midnight to compare with the election date.
+  const nowEt = toZonedTime(now, EASTERN_TIMEZONE)
+  const today = Date.UTC(nowEt.getFullYear(), nowEt.getMonth(), nowEt.getDate())
+  const daysToElection = Math.round((election.getTime() - today) / DAY_MS)
+  const smsCompliance: SmsComplianceWindow =
+    daysToElection < SMS_CUTOFF_LEAD_DAYS
+      ? 'closed'
+      : daysToElection < SMS_CUTOFF_LEAD_DAYS + SMS_CUTOFF_CLOSING_DAYS
+        ? 'closing'
+        : 'open'
+  return { smsCompliance, smsCutoffDate, generalElectionDate }
+}
